key_insight: UniX combines autoregressive and diffusion paradigms in a single design that avoids the typical parameter-sharing conflict, enabling both accurate semantic understanding (reports/labels) and high-fidelity chest X‑ray generation without compromising either task.
problem_solved: Current unified medical models force shared parameters across tasks with opposing objectives (semantic abstraction vs. pixel-level reconstruction), causing degraded performance; UniX resolves this tradeoff to jointly support reliable diagnosis-level outputs and realistic image synthesis.
method: Hybrid architecture that integrates autoregressive components for semantic/clinical output with diffusion-based decoders for pixel-accurate image generation while minimizing destructive parameter-sharing.
Task-specific heads or modular decoupling with a shared latent/encoder to preserve clinically relevant abstraction and enable high-quality reconstruction.
Cross-task consistency objectives and balanced training schedule to align semantics and appearance without one task dominating optimization.
impact: UniX enables a single foundation model to be used for both clinical chest X‑ray interpretation and realistic image generation, reducing model proliferation and simplifying workflows for research and deployment in medical imaging.

paper_title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
